problem: MLLM-based VLN agents process far more visual tokens than text tokens, making inference costly. Generic uniform token pruning ignores that historical and current frames play different roles in navigation.
motivation: Historical frames supply contextual memory and benefit from diversity, while the current frame drives the immediate action and needs saliency. A single uniform pruning rule therefore fits neither role well, and a task-aware strategy is needed to cut compute without hurting navigation.
key_idea: Asymmetric training-free token pruning for VLN: use a Determinantal Point Process to keep a diverse token subset in historical frames, and use the visual encoder's [CLS] attention to keep the most salient tokens in the current frame.
insight: Only the abstract was available, so no ablations can be cited. The abstract claims that matching the pruning criterion to the temporal role of each frame (diversity for history, saliency for the current view) maintains and often improves navigation performance while cutting computation.
method: Asymmetric pruning framework: applies different pruning strategies to historical and current frames, motivated by the temporal asymmetry of visual information in VLN.
DPP-based history pruning: uses a Determinantal Point Process to select a diverse subset of visual tokens from historical frames, preserving the trajectory context.
[CLS]-attention current-frame pruning: ranks current-frame tokens by the visual encoder's [CLS] attention and keeps the top salient ones for immediate action.
Training-free plug-in: applied to an already pre-trained MLLM-based VLN agent with no retraining.

setting.backbone: pre-trained MLLM-based VLN agent (unspecified in abstract), with pruning applied training-free
setting.training_data: none (training-free pruning on top of a pre-trained VLN agent)
setting.observation: egocentric RGB frames (current plus history); details not given in abstract

results: The abstract states that the method significantly reduces computational overhead while maintaining, and often improving, navigation performance on a pre-trained VLN agent. No quantitative results or baselines are given in the abstract.
limitations: Only the abstract was available, so benchmarks, backbone, and quantitative results could not be verified.
